extracted.intended_audience: Users of SINGULAR / computational algebraists (researchers or advanced users who work with toric ideals and semigroups)
extracted.subtask_description: Documentation for the cisimplicial SINGULAR library: procedures to test complete-intersection property of simplicial toric ideals and supporting semigroup/group routines (semigroup membership, minimal multiplier, group cardinality). Includes usage, assumptions and examples for each procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: cisimplicial.lib — Purpose / Overview
rubrics_metrics.description: Determines if the toric ideal of a simplicial toric variety is a complete intersection. A library for determining if a simplicial toric ideal is a complete intersection with NO NEED of computing explicitly a system of generators of such ideal. The procedures are based on two papers: I. Bermejo, I. Garcia-Marco and J.J. Salazar-Gonzalez: 'An algorithm for checking whether the toric ideal of an affine monomial curve is a complete intersection', J. Symbolic Computation 42 (2007) pags: 971–991 and I.Bermejo and I. Garcia-Marco: 'Complete intersections in simplicial toric varieties', Preprint (2010).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overview: Library intended to check complete-intersection property of simplicial toric ideals without computing generators. Authors: I.Bermejo, I.Garcia-Marco. Use the procedures in cisimplicial.lib; see individual procedure descriptions for usage, assumptions and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: minMult(a, b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Return: an integer k, the minimum positive integer such that k*a belongs to the semigroup generated by the integers in b.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: minMult (a, b); a integer, b integer vector. Assume: a is a positive integer, b is a vector of positive integers. Example: LIB "cisimplicial.lib"; int a = 46; intvec b = 13,17,59; minMult(a,b); => 3. Comment: "// 3*a = 8*b[1] + 2*b[2]". The function returns the smallest positive k with k*a in the semigroup <b>.

rubrics_metrics.name: belongSemigroup(v, A[, k])
rubrics_metrics.description: Return: counters, a vector with nonnegative entries such that A*counters = v. If it does not exist such a vector, it returns 0. If a third parameter k is introduced, it will only consider the first k columns of A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: belongSemigroup(v,A[,k]); v is an integral vector, A is an integral matrix, n is a positive integer. Assume: A is a matrix with nonnegative entries, nonzero columns, v is a nonnegative vector and nrows(v) = nrows(A). Examples (from docs): intmat A[3][4] = 10,3,2,1,2,1,1,3,5,0,1,2; intvec v = 23,12,10; belongSemigroup(v,A); => 1,3,1,2 with comment "// A * (1,3,1,2) = v". belongSemigroup(v,A,3); => 0 with comment "// v is not a combination of the first 3 columns of A". If target vector is not in the semigroup, returns 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: oneDimBelongSemigroup(n, v[, m])
rubrics_metrics.description: Return: counters, a vector with nonnegative entries such that v*counters = n. If it does not exist such a vector, it returns 0. If a third parameter m is introduced, it will only consider the first m entries of v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: oneDimBelongSemigroup(n,v[,m]); v is an integral vector, n is a positive integer[, m is a positive integer]. Assume: v is an integral vector with positive entries. Example: LIB "cisimplicial.lib"; int a = 95; intvec v = 18,51,13; oneDimBelongSemigroup(a,v); => 1,1,2 with comment "// 95 = 1*18 + 1*25 + 2*13". oneDimBelongSemigroup(a,v,2); => 0 with comment "// 95 is not a combination of 18 and 52;" (illustrates effect of limiting to first m entries).

rubrics_metrics.name: cardGroup(A[, n])
rubrics_metrics.description: It returns a bigint. If we denote by ZA the group generated by the columns of the matrix A, then it returns the number of elements of the group of Z^m / ZA, where m = number of rows of A. If a second parameter n is introduced, it will only consider the first n columns of A. It returns 0 if Z^m / ZA is infinite; this is, when rank ZA < m.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: cardGroup(A[,n]); A is a matrix with integral coefficients. Return: a bigint equal to |Z^m / ZA| when finite; returns 0 when the quotient is infinite (i.e., rank ZA < m). Use second parameter to restrict to first n columns. No explicit example printed here, but notes explain behavior when group is infinite vs finite.
